sheets.title: The syllable chart
sheets.intro: Maya scribes wrote with about 80 syllable signs, each a consonant plus a vowel. This chart shows one clear form of each, drawn by David Stuart. Keep it beside you for the other sheets. Empty squares are syllables with no securely known sign.

sheets.title: First signs
sheets.intro: Write the sound of each sign on the line. Start with the five vowels, then use the chart for the rest.

sheets.title: More signs
sheets.intro: Write the sound of each sign. Look at the inside details as well as the outline: many signs share the same rounded frame.

sheets.title: Find the sign
sheets.intro: Circle the sign that spells the sound on the left. One of the wrong choices is often a sign that looks very like the right one.

sheets.title: One sound, many signs
sheets.intro: Scribes could spell the same syllable with different signs. Every sign here spells one of these six sounds: a, u, ma, ji, ka, na. Write the sound under each.

sheets.title: Read a word
sheets.intro: Maya words are spelled syllable by syllable, and the vowel of the last syllable is usually not spoken: ka-ka-wa is read kakaw, “cacao”. Write the syllables, then the word. The meanings are in the box, in a different order.

sheets.title: Write a word
sheets.intro: Spell each word with signs from the chart, one sign per box. All five words are carved at Palenque, and you will meet them again on the last sheet.

sheets.title: Copy the signs
sheets.intro: Draw each sign three times, saying its sound aloud. Copy the outline first, then the details inside. Drawing a sign is the fastest way to remember it.

sheets.title: Tell them apart
sheets.intro: Each pair is two different syllables that beginners often mix up. Write the sound under each sign, then circle the detail that tells them apart. Use the syllable chart to check.

sheets.title: Word signs
sheets.intro: Some signs stand for a whole word. Match each sign to its meaning from the box. Look for the picture in the sign: the macaw’s beak, the jaguar’s spots, the tree’s grain.

sheets.title: Bars and dots
sheets.intro: A dot is one and a bar is five, so three bars and two dots make seventeen. The shell is zero. Write each number, then draw the numbers in part B.

sheets.title: Numbers at Palenque
sheets.intro: These blocks are carved on the Cross Group tablets at Palenque. Each begins with a bar-and-dot number, set beside or above the main sign. Write the number. The curls and crescents beside the dots are fillers that keep the block square, and they are not counted.

sheets.title: Read at Palenque
sheets.intro: Each block spells one word with syllable signs only. The signs you need are in the strip below, but on the tablets they are squeezed, turned and joined together. Find them in the block, then write the syllables and the word. Read a block left to right, then top to bottom.
